title: Prof. Daniel Kahneman: Art & Science of Decision Making
description: This video with Daniel Kahneman (Nobel Prize in Economics) explores how we make decisions, what leads us to good or bad choices, cognitive biases, etc.

title: Video 1: Decision Analysis 1 - Maximax, Maximin, Minimax Regret
description: The video explains three approaches to decision-making without using probabilities — Maximax (optimistic), Maximin (conservative), and Minimax Regret — applying them step-by-step to a practical example of financial investments.

title: Video 2: Decision Analysis 1.1 (Costs) - Optimistic, Conservative, Minimax Regre
description: This video explains how to make cost-based decisions without using probabilities by applying the optimistic, conservative, and minimax regret approaches

title: Decision Analysis 1b: Equally Likely (Laplace) and Realism (Hurwicz)
description: This video explains how to evaluate investment decisions without probabilities by applying the equally likely (Laplace) and realism (Hurwicz) approaches

title: Decision Analysis 3: Decision Trees
description: This video tutorial demonstrates how to construct and solve a basic decision tree using the expected value approach to evaluate and choose the best investment alternative

title: How to analyze decision situations using Decision Tree
description: This video explains how to use decision trees to visually analyze multi-stage decision problems and calculate expected monetary values to determine the optimal course of action

title: Heuristics and Biases in Decision Making, explained
description: We all use heuristics to make everyday decisions — but sometimes they blind us to the truth. Therefore, we need to do something that isn't easy: accept that our ideas might be wrong.

title: Video 1: How to Forecast with Confidence Using Monte Carlo Simulation | The Statistical CFO
description: The video demonstrates how CFOs and finance professionals can utilize Monte Carlo simulation to transition from instinct-based estimating to data-driven probability distributions, enabling them to confidently forecast financial outcomes and clearly communicate risks to stakeholders

title: Video 2: Monte Carlo Simulation Explained. Why Single Forecasts Mislead Decision Makers
description: This video explains why relying on single-number forecasts can be dangerously misleading, and introduces the Monte Carlo simulation as a powerful tool that explores thousands of possible futures to help decision-makers better understand and manage risk and uncertainty

title: Monte Carlo Simulation Made Super Easy!
description: This video provides a step-by-step guide on how to perform a 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation in Excel for a basic income statement, utilizing randomized functions and data tables to determine expected profit and calculate the probability of a financial loss

title: Group Decision Making Techniques
description: The video demonstrates practical techniques that groups can use to improve their decision-making.

title: Video 1: The Essence of Real Option
description: This video explains how real option pricing can augment traditional discounted cash flow valuation by factoring in the value of learning and adaptive behavior, provided that the business decision meets the strict criteria of having an embedded option, possessing exclusivity, and satisfying the basic principles required to use these pricing model

title: Data Model in Excel - What is it? What is it used for?
description: Did you know that the "Data Model" feature can help you create pivot tables by merging data sources? With this tool, you can efficiently load and organize your data, allowing you to create customized queries for analysis and decision-making. In this video, we'll explore what the Data Model in Excel is and what it's used for—a tool that facilitates the organization and analysis of information for Business Intelligence professionals.
